description: A diagnostic slot that reproduces another game's spheres to surface logic leaks.

logic-test-0.1.0.description:
Initial release of **Logic Test**, a diagnostic Archipelago world for surfacing logic leaks in another game's world.

## What it does

Add one Logic Test slot alongside one or more games-under-test. During generation it generates the under-test slots together as one nested multiworld, reads their overall (cross-game) sphere structure, and rebuilds itself as a linear chain of gated spheres matching it:

- Every under-test item is pulled out and locked into a Logic Test sphere location.
- Each under-test location instead receives a `KEY_i` macguffin.
- Sphere `i` only opens once the slot has collected every `KEY_i`, releasing that sphere's original items.

Play is forced into lock-step with the intended spheres, so every check matters. A logic leak (an access rule looser in the model than the real game) shows up as a hard stall: a key the model says is reachable but isn't, so the next sphere never opens.

## Setup

Add one Logic Test slot plus one or more games-under-test. Slot order does not matter, since each under-test game's RNG is reproduced from its slot number, so YAMLs can be in any order.

## Limits

- Up to 512 spheres
- Up to 100,000 locations (networkable items across all under-test games)

## Assets

- `logic_test.apworld`: the world, install it into your Archipelago `custom_worlds` directory
- `Logic.Test.yaml`: a template options YAML

Requires Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer.

logic-test-0.1.1.description:
Bugfix release.

- **Priority/early items no longer leak into the under-test games.** Locations locked by priority or early-item fill were mistaken for fixed placements and got no `KEY`, so the outer fill dropped real items onto them, sometimes failing generation. They now become normal `KEY` targets.
- **Unreachable markers (reverse-leak detector).** Under-test locations the model can't reach in progression now get a `Logic Test Unreachable Marker` instead of a `KEY`. Picking one up means the real game reached what the model proved unreachable. Only appears under `minimal`/`items` accessibility.

Assets: `logic_test.apworld` (install into `custom_worlds`) and `Logic.Test.yaml`. Requires Archipelago 0.6.7+.

logic-test-0.2.0.description:
## Logic Test 0.2.0

### WebHost slot launch
- Clicking a **Logic Test** slot on a WebHost room page now opens the Logic Test Client instead of the generic Text Client, when the apworld is installed. The client auto-connects using the room's `archipelago://` link.
- If the Logic Test apworld isn't installed, behavior is unchanged: the slot falls back to the Text Client. Fully backwards compatible with existing rooms.

### Other
- Added an MIT license.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/palex00/Archipelago/compare/logic-test-0.1.1...logic-test-0.2.0

logic-test-0.2.1.description:
## Logic Test 0.2.1

Bugfix release for the WebHost slot launch added in 0.2.0.

### Fixes
- **Selecting the Logic Test Client from the WebHost slot picker now actually opens it.** The launcher passes the room's `archipelago://` URI to the client, but the launch handler dropped it — raising a `TypeError` and silently failing, so nothing happened when you picked the client. It now accepts and forwards the URI, and the client auto-connects as intended.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/palex00/Archipelago/compare/logic-test-0.2.0...logic-test-0.2.1

logic-test-0.3.0.description:
## Sphere model fix: locked placements no longer break lock-step

Fixed the bug where locked in-game placements in the under-test game (vanilla or shuffled badges, HMs, key items) caused interleaved keys — e.g. lots of `KEY_12` arriving while `KEY_11` was still incomplete — along with false `LOGIC LEAK` warnings in the client. These items are never gated by the KEY spheres, so the player picks them up mid-sphere in real play; the sphere model now collects them via closure (like events) in both `count_events` modes, restoring the lock-step guarantee: a `KEY_(i+1)` is never legitimately reachable before every `KEY_i`.

Related hardening:
- The unreachable-marker pass uses the same networkable-location predicate as the sphere computation.
- Generation fails loudly if the fixed-location snapshot hook didn't run, instead of silently falling back to post-fill lock flags.
- Non-advancement items are skipped in the closure sets (they can't affect reachability).
- New regression test replays gated play via `MultiWorld.get_spheres` against a slot with shuffled (locked) badges/HMs.

## Client improvements

- **Leak tracking persists across reconnects**: keys received ahead of the current sphere are recorded in server data storage (per team/slot), so leak history survives reconnects and item replays. Leaked spheres are flagged in the status output and GUI with the sphere they arrived on.
- **Per-sphere key totals**: the status list and GUI tab now show have/required key counts for every sphere (done / now / locked), not just the current one.

## Upgrade notes

Seeds generated with 0.2.1 or earlier keep their old (misgrouped) key assignment — the fix applies at generation time, so affected multiworlds need a regen. Existing games remain playable; the early keys are safe and the leak warnings they trigger are spurious.
